title: Cheese and bacon scones with grape compote

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is plain home-kitchen fare: flour, butter, cheddar, bacon, yoghurt, milk, grapes, honey, cinnamon and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, bowl, baking tray and small pan, and rubbing in and patting out scone dough is beginner technique.

works.reason: The flour-to-yoghurt-and-milk ratio gives a workable scone dough, 220°C for 15 to 18 minutes suits a scone round, and 400g of grapes plus yoghurt and eight scones feeds four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty-five active minutes covers frying the bacon, rubbing in, shaping, halving the grapes and minding the compote while the scones bake for the stated 18 minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: The 400g of grapes are a full component of the plate rather than a garnish, and warm scones with a hot compote suit a November morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Scones with cheese and bacon, plus fruit and Greek yoghurt, make a proper filling breakfast with protein and fruit.
